name: Worlds Upon The Wind
one_liner: Releases a Steam deckbuilder's full source and art as public domain.

text.why: Commercial game code is rarely visible, so indie developers seldom see how a finished game is built. Worlds Upon The Wind, a peaceful roguelite deckbuilder sold on Steam, releases its whole Godot project under CC0: GDScript source, PSD and SVG art, and the Steam build and publish scripts. The art is based on public-domain Japanese ukiyo-e prints and picture scrolls. Music and sound effects are excluded for licensing reasons, so a build from the repository runs silent.
text.take: Unlike a tutorial, this is a finished, selling game you can take apart in full.
build: A structural reference for your own Godot 4 game
A card-game UI mock-up built on public-domain woodblock prints
A sample of scripts that automate multi-platform Steam releases

who.situation: building a first commercial-scale Godot project
wants to see source PSDs and print-based art in use

start.text: Install Godot 4.7, then Import wutw/project.godot from the Project Manager
If console errors appear, wait for the import to finish and reopen
Press F5 to run · music and SFX are excluded, so only cutscene voice plays

caveat: Music and sound effects excluded; a repo build runs silent
A read-only mirror: pull requests are not merged
Dictionary and sentence data carry separate CC-BY-SA-style licenses

license.scope_text: Public domain. Use, change, redistribute; no notice needed.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.
